title: Spain Declares First-Ever Wildfire National Emergency as Blazes Sweep Southern Europe
excerpt: Tens of thousands flee as wildfires rage across Spain, France, and Italy amid Europe's worst fire season in years, with France invoking EU emergency aid.
body:
• Spain declared its first-ever national emergency linked to a wildfire on Thursday night, as blazes near Madrid and Avila forced the evacuation of more than 10,000 people.
  • France requested EU civil protection aid on Friday after a fast-moving wildfire near Bordeaux displaced over 10,000 residents and tourists overnight.
  • More than 100,000 hectares have burned in Spain in 2026, matching the country's entire annual average for the past decade, with 13 deaths this season.
  • Scientists say Europe is warming at twice the global average, with three successive heatwaves this summer drying vegetation into fuel for wildfires.

Spain's Unprecedented Emergency Declaration

The Spanish government on Thursday night declared a national emergency after wildfires threatened communities near Madrid and in the neighbouring province of Avila — the first time Spain has invoked such a declaration for a wildfire, according to Reuters.

https://x.com/Osint613/status/2080419901827653645

The Interior Ministry said the decision was driven by the simultaneous outbreak of several fires, adverse weather, and the need to mobilise resources from multiple administrations. Active fires in Villa del Prado, San Martín de Valdeiglesias, and Almorox had the potential to advance beyond current extinguishing capacity, the Madrid regional government said, describing the situation as one of "extreme gravity."

More than 10,000 people were evacuated from four towns west of Madrid. Authorities deployed over 270 emergency personnel, 40 ground units, and several Military Emergency Unit (UME) contingents. Under Spain's civil protection law, the declaration places the response under the direct authority of the interior minister.

The emergency came as a separate, massive wildfire in Guadalajara province — Spain's largest this year at 32,000 hectares — continued to burn. That blaze, the second-largest on record in the country's history, forced the evacuation of 34 villages and consumed 90% of a national park, according to CNN.

"Year after year we clearly see how climate change kills and destroys wealth in our communities. This isn't politics. It is science, it's about facts."

— Pedro Sánchez, Prime Minister of Spain

France Seeks EU Aid as Bordeaux-Area Fire Spreads

French President Emmanuel Macron on Friday announced that France had requested the activation of the European Union's civil protection mechanism to combat a major wildfire near the Atlantic coast.

"The situation remains extremely tense with the fires hitting our country, particularly in Gironde," Macron wrote on X. Reinforcements — two Croatian Canadair aircraft, two Portuguese Air Tractor planes, and two Black Hawk helicopters from the Czech Republic and Slovakia — were on their way, he said.

A fast-moving wildfire near Lège-Cap-Ferret, west of Bordeaux, had ripped through at least 2,400 hectares overnight, forcing the evacuation of more than 10,000 people, including tourists from campsites on the Arcachon Bay peninsula, according to Reuters. Five hundred firefighters battled the blaze.

France has suffered a devastating fire season: 44,000 hectares burned so far, well above average. Two firefighters died earlier this week near Bordeaux Airport. Macron said France had "never faced so many outbreaks of fire since the end of World War II." Separately, France's public health agency reported that a record heatwave in June caused an estimated 5,700 excess deaths.

A Continent Under Fire

The crises extend across southern Europe. In Sicily, firefighters have conducted more than 1,000 operations since Saturday, with a 59-year-old firefighter dying while battling a blaze near San Cataldo. Greece sweltered under a four-day heatwave with temperatures above 42°C, while Cyprus issued warnings for 43°C highs.

Spain is the EU's most fire-affected country in 2026, with 104,423 hectares burned, according to the EU's Copernicus wildfire monitoring service. Thirteen people have died, including foreign nationals killed in a blaze in Almeria province earlier this month. Scientists say abundant vegetation growth after heavy spring rain has dried out in extreme summer heat, creating fuel for rapidly spreading fires. Europe is the world's fastest-warming continent, with temperatures rising at twice the global average since the 1980s.

Travel Advisory for Indian Visitors

Spain and France rank among the most popular European summer destinations for Indian tourists. With fires disrupting transport, closing roads, and degrading air quality, travellers should monitor conditions closely. The Almeria fire killed several foreign nationals, underscoring risks in fire-prone areas. Travellers are advised to register with the Indian embassy or consulate at their destination.

What's Next

Spain's weather agency AEMET has warned that wildfire danger remains "very high or extreme" across most of the mainland. A brief cooldown Friday may be short-lived, with temperatures forecast to surge again from Sunday. Firefighters in Guadalajara hope to contain Spain's largest active blaze by Friday, but authorities caution the season's most critical period has not yet arrived.
nri_angle: Spain and France are top European summer destinations for Indian tourists, and the wildfires pose risks to travellers through transport disruptions, road closures, and degraded air quality.
